_meta.source: Teks asli heartodex (descriptionOriginal di file data) dengan salah ketik yang jelas dibetulkan. descriptionOriginal tetap apa adanya.

cabbage-white: Its gray-white wings make it low-key in daily life.
large-red-damselfly: It's a vibrant damselfly that loves to dance by the water.
european-firebug: Its unique red-and-black coloring earned it a spot on the cover of an entomology journal!
asparagus-beetle: It's a dull-colored little bug, commonly found in flower fields.
gold-grasshopper: With long, sturdy antennae, it can sense changes in its surroundings with ease.
apollo: With its furry coat, it seems unafraid of the cold.
orange-tip: With bright markings on its wings, it's a frequent visitor to the town.
common-brimstone: With its unique colors and patterns, it flutters around the Suburbs no matter the weather.
old-world-swallowtail: Because of its alluring beauty, it got nicknames like "Flying Flower" and "Insect Artist."
postman-butterfly: Don't be too focused on the two red spots. This butterfly as a whole is a piece of art.
sulkowskys-morpho: Its wings are thin as silk, gleaming with a pearly luster and radiant light.
bumblebee: Its body is chunky, like a little bear who just filled its belly.
green-tiger-beetle: Its back shimmers with a metallic sheen, like jade armor.
wasp-beetle: It relies on masterful disguise skills to mimic a hornet and move freely through the forest.
amethyst-flower-beetle: Its shell is a vibrant blue-purple, and it prefers humid weather.
siberian-grasshopper: It's found in Fishing Village, and its hockey-stick-shaped antennae and giant forelegs are truly a marvel.
four-spotted-skimmer: Perching high like a fighter, its four black wing spots are the mark of its renown.
common-blue-butterfly: It often flutters its dazzling blue wings, dancing through the town.
seven-spotted-ladybug: It's a ladybug with three more spots than a four-spotted one. Seeing it is said to bring good luck.
waroona-cuckoo-bee: Gray-and-white stripes line up on its tail. Did it get inspiration from a zebra?
fire-colored-beetle: Its whole body is fuming red! Guess it's an onsen lover.
ant: Ants are scaling high, clouds on the hill—heavy rain is coming soon.
rajah-brookes-birdwing: The red spots on its body are its most distinctive feature, and it's occasionally seen near homes.
purple-emperor: Out of a love for purple, it taught itself light-and-shadow magic to change the color of its wings.
mini-moon-moth: Its Morandi hues give it an elegant and refined beauty.
katydid: It loves to sing whenever it's happy.
pink-katydid: Its gorgeous skin wasn't won by tumbling into a jar of strawberry jam.
cicada: After waiting so long underground, it's now making itself heard—loud and clear!
large-banded-grasshopper: With vivid red hind legs, it prefers bright and sunny weather.
common-whitetail: It prefers humid weather, commonly found near rivers.
mediterranean-mantis: It may look normal, but it's got rainbows under its wings!
beautiful-leopard: It's a butterfly of fashion dressed in a natural leopard-print coat.
four-spotted-ladybug: It's a ladybug with three fewer spots than a seven-spotted one, and it lives by the warm lakeside.
splay-footed-carpenter: Its wings shimmer with a purple sheen, and it prefers to dwell in places of scenic beauty.
alpine-longhorn-beetle: It's a picky little bug with extraordinarily long antennae, only appearing on rainbow days.
giant-asian-mantis: A formidable mantis, armed with two axe-like forelimbs, is always ready to fight.
mourning-cloak: It loves sunny weather and warm places, and its wings shine a bright orange-yellow hue.
peacock-butterfly: The eyespots on its wings shimmer with a mysterious glow, said to scare off predators.
asian-lady-beetle: The spots on its back form a perfect smiley face. What a wonderful personality!
beautiful-demoiselle: It's a darker-colored damselfly that carries a sense of maturity as if it sees through the world.
blue-shieldbug: It looks like a flying sapphire that follows a regular schedule, emerging only on daylight.
silver-jewel-scarab: Dazzling as if covered in jewels, it's obviously from a rich family.
stag-beetle: Some call it "Flying Deer." It's very true for the flying part.
green-birdwing: Its metallic green wings look like bright sunlight shining through leaves.
golden-jewel-scarab: A gold coin sprouted wings and flew away... Oh, it's just a bug.
elegant-flower-beetle: Who gave it that name? Though it is charmingly vibrant, naming itself "Elegant" feels a bit too on the nose.
minotaur-beetle: It's gentle and harmless by nature, but its horns atop the head pack a powerful punch.
crimson-marsh-glider: Like a radiant rose in full bloom, it appears only beneath the rainbow.
blue-morpho: Living in dense forests, its blue wings are strikingly beautiful.
chestnut-tiger: Beyond its toxins, its vivid colors warn passing birds not to provoke it.
picasso-bug: Its back bears abstract, intricate patterns, signaling that it's a stylish yet formidable bug.
horned-beetle: It holds a powerful double-headed horn on its head, and it prefers to crawl in the dark at midnight and dawn.
spanish-moon-moth: It's a beautiful yet short-lived, making every sighting a moment to cherish.
comet-moth: With two long ribbons trailing from its wingtips, it looks like a comet streaking across the sky as it flies.
cerulean-carpenter: It shows up only on rainbow days, perhaps craving more than just blue.
rainbow-stag-beetle: If you manage to catch it, you will hold a little piece of rainbow in your palm.
golden-stag-beetle: It shines with a golden hue, exuding an aura of luxury and elegance.
conehead-mantis: This mantis has a protrusion from its crown, strange in appearance but hard to spot.
mother-of-pearl: After living long among flower fields, it has taken on a delicate, floral pink-purple hue.
hercules-beetle: It's small in size but mighty in strength, said to be able to lift objects many times its own weight.
sunset-morpho: Its color easily evokes the magnificent scene of sunrise, and the place it inhabits is the best spot to watch it.
morpho-helena: Wing flaps resemble white waves on a deep blue sea—worthy of the name of Helena.
bagworm-moth: It's an insect architect that builds its own house using branches and leaves.
orchid-mantis: Posing like an elegant orchid, this born hunter takes pride in its deadly mimicry
brown-rhinoceros-beetle: Brown grooves like ancient totems carved into its shell, plus a sickle-shaped horn—this one means business.
iridescent-rhinoceros-beetle: With its festive patterned markings, it charges forward like a tiny, colorful bulldozer.
grey-horned-firefly: The gray-green tones give it a calm, steady look, helping it navigate its surroundings through the pits on its antennae.
purple-horned-firefly: That deep purple "glow face" is hard to miss—it stands out even in the dark.
pink-horned-firefly: A two-step courtship routine—pink glow and sensitive antennae—gives it a much better shot at finding a mate.
white-banded-erebus-moth: Giant demon-eye markings—perfect for scaring off any predator looking for a bite.
blue-milkweed-beetle: Its colors are as dreamy as the northern lights, yet this well-known foodie has its favorite meal written right in its name.
agrias-butterfly: As a strong flying butterfly, its thoracic muscles are remarkably well-developed—you can tell just from its wing markings.
morpho-luna: A cool, ethereal blue—every wingbeat carries the grace of a goddess.
green-flower-chafer: An emerald gem of a butterfly that spends its days perched in the treetops.
yellow-brick-large-red-damselfly: A toy large red damselfly made of yellow bricks. Will its vibrant colors attract even more insects?
blue-brick-large-red-damselfly: A toy large red damselfly made of blue bricks. When it dances by the water, will tiny specks drift down?
purple-brick-large-red-damselfly: A toy large red damselfly made of purple bricks—proudly showing off its noble modular armor.
pink-brick-large-red-damselfly: A toy large red damselfly made of pink bricks—shedding its usual rough-and-tumble image, now radiating gentle charm.
golden-script-supervisor-bumblebee: A smart script supervisor resembling a golden bumblebee, just wrapped on the film Gold Rush.
purple-script-supervisor-bumblebee: A smart script supervisor resembles a purple bumblebee. When glitching, it buzzes wildly as if in a musical scene.
red-script-supervisor-bumblebee: A smart script supervisor resembles a red bumblebee, meticulously noting every detail of horror movie scenes.
pink-script-supervisor-bumblebee: A smart script supervisor resembles a pink bumblebee, a busy fixture on romance film sets.
green-script-supervisor-bumblebee: A smart script supervisor resembles a green bumblebee, occasionally making cameo appearances in nature documentaries.
frostspore-queen-alexandras-birdwing: A Frostspore-infected Queen Alexandra's Birdwing, so delicate it seems it might shatter at a touch.
frostspore-postman-butterfly: A Frostspore-infected Postman Butterfly, its markings now glowing like neon strips along its wings.
frostspore-purple-spotted-swallowtail: A Frostspore-infected Purple Spotted Swallowtail, its dreamy new look is a world apart from its former self.
frostspore-mother-of-pearl: A Frostspore-infected Mother-of-Pearl, now resembling a precious butterfly gem brooch.
frostspore-sulkowskys-morpho: A Frostspore-infected Sulkowsky's Morpho, with wings so translucent they refract light into an even more dazzling display.
